title: I Raised the Wrong Fiancé
synopsis: Arrogant Tristan Sterling didn't want a "country bumpkin" from Wyoming as his fiancée. To force a breakup, he pays the school’s brokest scholarship student, Asher, to pretend to be him. Ivy Vance falls for the deception completely. She showers Asher with her endless fortune, personal protection, and unyielding affection. But when Tristan realizes Ivy is actually stunning, he steps in to claim his rightful place. Except Ivy looks him dead in the eye and asks: "Who the hell are you?"
intro: Tristan Sterling does not want a fiancée from Wyoming, so he pays Asher, the school's brokest scholarship student, to pretend to be him. It reads like a romantic comedy novel, now on screen: Ivy Vance falls for the stand-in, showers him with her fortune, protection and affection, and the arrogant original only notices what he gave away when it is too late. The whole story builds to one line Ivy delivers straight to his face.
why: A swapped-fiancé romance where the plan backfires on the person who made it.
Ivy Vance is generous, rich and nobody's fool, which makes the payoff land.
Good pick if you like arrogant leads getting exactly what they asked for.

faq.q: Is I Raised the Wrong Fiancé worth watching?
faq.a: If you like romantic comedies built on a deception that blows up, yes. It is light and focused on the moment Tristan tries to take his place back.
Ivy Vance, the fiancée from Wyoming; Tristan Sterling, the fiancé who tried to get out of the engagement; and Asher, the scholarship student paid to pretend to be him.
